title: Swap-only instances turn the Instance Configuration Document into a registry of trading routes, not just capital deployments
content:
Three Curve instances declare `Asset Supplied By Spark Liquidity Layer` as "N/A - swap only": USDC/USDT (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.7.2.2.1.3), weETH/WETH-ng "for Swaps" (.7.5.2.1.3) and rlUSD/USDC "for Swaps" (.7.6.2.1.3). Their inflow and outflow rate limits carry the same string in place of numbers (.7.2.2.4.1/.2, .7.5.2.4.1/.2, .7.6.2.4.1/.2), leaving only the swap leg populated.

These instances hold no position. Spark never supplies liquidity to the pool and never receives an LP token to hold; the venue is used as an exchange and nothing more. The `Token` field still lists an LP token (`crv2pool`) because the template demands one, but it names the pool rather than a holding.

That makes the Instance Configuration Document do double duty. For lending and vault venues it records *where the balance sheet is deployed*; for these it records *which routes the Relayer may trade through*, sized by how much and at what maximum slippage. Both live in the same tree under the same `Active` status, distinguished only by the N/A markers.

The governance consequence is worth being explicit about: authorising a swap route is materially different from authorising a deployment. There is no ongoing counterparty exposure to monitor, but there is a standing permission to move value through a third-party pool, whose worst case is execution loss rather than principal loss. Filing both under one schema keeps the approval process uniform, at the cost of letting a reader assume every `Active` instance represents capital at risk in that venue.
description: Curve USDC/USDT, weETH/WETH-ng and rlUSD/USDC record Asset Supplied By Spark Liquidity Layer as 'N/A - swap only' with both inflow and outflow legs disabled, leaving swap limits as the only live
